summary: Code review PASS for WP-008 (Branch API Routes).

src/server/routes/branches.ts: The most complex of the four route files. Two handlers with meaningfully different concerns: a GET that delegates to an async orchestrator and a POST that validates rich input then delegates to another async orchestrator method.
Architecture: workspace existence validation via workspaceManager.getById() precedes git I/O in both handlers — correct fast-fail design that avoids wasting git operations on invalid coordinates.

GET handler: correct Map-to-plain-object conversion (lines 80–83) for JSON serialisation. BranchesResponse interface is exported and imported in the test — prevents silent schema drift across the test boundary. The fallback catch maps any orchestrator exception to 404; this is slightly broad (a real orchestrator failure would be a 500), but as the only documented error path from getAvailableBranches() is 'project does not exist' (a 404-worthy condition), this is pragmatically correct for current usage.

POST handler: validates assignments field thoroughly — must be a plain object (not array), non-empty, and all values must be string. This is the most complete input validation of all four route files. The per-entry check (lines 141–146) correctly identifies which key had the invalid value in the error message.

POST switchBranches() catch maps to 500 (line 154). This is the only 500 in any route file and is appropriate: a switch failure is an internal/git error, not a client error. The test gap (no test for the 500 path) is low-risk as noted by QA.

setImmediate vs nextTick for async flush: GET tests correctly use setImmediate (full event loop tick) to drain the Promise microtask queue from getAvailableBranches(), while POST tests use two process.nextTick calls (sufficient for parseJsonBody + synchronous mock resolution). Both are correct for their respective async depths.

Test file: MockBranchOrchestrator with configurable stubs (setBranchMap, setSwitchResult, setThrowOnGet, setThrowOnSwitch) is the most flexible mock in the suite — well-designed for future coverage additions. MockWorkspaceManager uses a lean registerWorkspace/setThrowOnGet approach. 12 tests cover 4 GET paths and 8 POST paths.
495/495 tests pass. All 5 ACs confirmed met.

comments.note: isPlainObject() defined locally in branches.ts — fourth instance of the same 3-line helper across route files. At this point extraction to requestUtils.ts is clearly warranted and should be done as a follow-up refactor.

GET handler catch block (line 87-89) maps any orchestrator exception to 404. For the current BranchOrchestrator implementation this is correct (the only documented throw is 'project does not exist'). If orchestrator errors grow (e.g., git I/O failures), this would incorrectly surface as 404. A future improvement: distinguish NotFoundError from other errors, mapping git failures to 500.

MockBranchOrchestrator.setThrowOnSwitch() is implemented in the test file but never called by any test, leaving the POST 500 path uncovered. This is a known gap from QA. The infrastructure to cover it is already present — adding one test would be trivial.

notes: All 5 ACs met. 495/495 tests pass. Both routes covered. Minor untested 500 path in POST switch. Clean for code review.
